The facility, which aims to eventually comprise roughly 1 million GPUs, utilizes closed-loop liquid cooling and advanced networking to optimize performance. Meta reports achieving more than 85% goodput for pre-training and over 90% for reinforcement learning runs. Through rigorous engineering, the company reduced interruption rates by 99% compared to the initial phase peak, stabilizing operations for large-scale training jobs. The supercluster currently deploys NVIDIA GB200 and GB300 platforms, with future expansion planned for the Vera Rubin architecture. This infrastructure supports Meta's goal of delivering new AI experiences to billions of people.
items.title: Meta Unveils Prometheus Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster for AI Training

items.summary: Negotiators struggle to finalize a US-India trade pact due to US tariff challenges, energy import disputes, and improved US ties with Pakistan. Secretary of State Marco Rubio visits Mumbai and Jamnagar to address investment and energy issues, bypassing the capital. Experts cite legal uncertainty over US tariffs and India's caution regarding new trade measures as primary hurdles preventing an agreement.
items.title: US-India Trade Deal Faces Delays Amid Tariff and Energy Friction

items.summary: Anthropic exposed a robust network of approximately 70 AI-powered fake news sites that generated at least 318 articles regarding the conflict in eastern DRC, relations with Rwanda, and mineral resources. The operation, attributed to the French agency LKM Company, coordinated accounts on X to amplify content while mimicking legitimate media. While no direct government involvement was found, the campaign significantly weakened DRC's diplomatic standing and fueled hatred against Rwandans. Local journalists face severe constraints, including lack of resources and unstable internet, making verification difficult. The revelation highlights the challenges fact-checkers face in distinguishing malicious disinformation from legitimate criticism amidst strained regional security.
items.title: Anthropic Exposes AI Disinformation Network Targeting DRC

items.summary: Jonathan Vogel demonstrates calculating trade gains using home-foreign elasticity functions rather than constant elasticity. Estimated functions show median gains of 19.37 log points across WIOD countries, compared to 24.43 when elasticities remain fixed. The study uses tariff changes from trade agreements for identification.
items.title: Jonathan Vogel Analyzes Trade Gains via Elasticity Functions

items.summary: A study finds mortgage intermediaries captured over 60% of $1.5 billion in GSE fee waivers during 2023–2024. Officers with expensive loan histories passed through less than 20%, retaining incentives to steer borrowers into higher-rate mortgages despite regulations.
items.title: Loan Officers Capture Most GSE Fee Waiver Savings

items.summary: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi strongly denied claims that she is driving a weak yen and high interest rates, stating she categorically rejects such accusations made in Parliament. Her administration aims to boost confidence through fiscal sustainability and appropriate bond issuance control. While market unease persists regarding fiscal management, officials like Growth Strategy Minister Minoru Kiuchi and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama have also downplayed reflationary policies. Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda noted underlying inflation is near the 2% target.
items.title: Japan PM Denies Responsibility for Weak Yen and High Rates

items.summary: The Nasdaq rose Monday as investors rotated back into chip stocks, following last week's selloff fueled by fears over the sustainability of the AI boom. Momentum in the AI trade continues as investors await Wednesday's earnings report from Meta, which has gained in AI through massive investments. Market volatility has delayed several tech IPOs, though investors remain discerning about weakness.
items.title: Nasdaq Rises as Investors Return to AI Stocks Ahead of Meta Earnings

items.summary: Mumbai Police have deferred the night transfer of three accused from Kota to Mumbai in the Tiger Shroff firing case due to security concerns. The suspects remain under heavy guard at the Railway Colony police station, which has been turned into a high-security zone. Investigators are examining their roles and alleged escape routes, while the accused face charges including an attempt-to-murder case and offences under the Arms Act.
items.title: Mumbai Police Defer Transfer of Tiger Shroff Accused Due to Security Concerns

items.summary: A study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences suggests that brief aerobic exercise or a 90-minute nap can help preserve memory formation after 30 hours of sleep deprivation. Researchers found both interventions improved performance by around 22% compared to a control group, though the difference between exercise and napping was not statistically significant. The findings apply to healthy young adults in laboratory settings.
items.title: Aerobic Exercise and Naps May Counteract Memory Loss from Sleep Deprivation

items.summary: Although Doppler Labs ceased operations in 2017, its vision for in-ear computing persists. Founded in 2013, the company aimed to create advanced wireless earbuds with features like real-time translation and audio mixing. Apple's AirPods, released in December 2016 and updated in 2019, eventually fulfilled many of Doppler's original goals, shipping 16.8 million units in a single quarter.
items.title: Doppler Labs' Failed Startup Vision Lives On in Apple AirPods

items.summary: Tejaji Nagar police in Indore busted a three-member gang allegedly involved in daytime burglaries of locked houses. Two youths, Ajay Yogi and Altamash Mohammad, were arrested, while a minor was detained. Police recovered a gold mangalsutra, silver anklets, bangles, and a motorcycle, estimating the value at around Rs 3 lakh. The gang allegedly conducted reconnaissance during the day before breaking locks and stealing valuables.
items.title: Police Busted Burglary Gang in Indore Recovering Valuables

items.summary: Persistent severe weather conditions, including heat waves and droughts, pose significant risks to critical infrastructure, homes, and lives in the U.S. and worldwide. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) noted 2023 as the fifth-warmest year in the country's 129-year record. Extreme heat strains power grids, causing inefficiencies and potential outages. Interruptions in healthcare, manufacturing, and data centers incur substantial hourly costs. To mitigate these risks, organizations are urged to adopt continuous monitoring solutions that provide real-time insights, enabling proactive maintenance and preventing costly downtime during extreme weather events.
items.title: Severe Weather Threatens Critical Infrastructure Operations Globally

items.summary: An oil well in southern Niger has been spewing crude oil and gas since Sept. 25, damaging installations and threatening nearby wildlife. Authorities stated the situation remains uncontrolled four weeks later. Abdoulkarim Mohamed Ali of Niger's Ministry of Petroleum described the incident as exceptionally severe, noting oil ejected over 10 meters. Investigations are ongoing to determine the cause and responsibility, with no criminal or terrorist intent found.
items.title: Severe Oil Well Eruption in Niger Threatens Desert Wildlife

items.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season following a diagnosis of blood clots in both lungs. According to his team and agent, the 28-year-old was hospitalized in London until 4am on game day. While his prognosis is considered very good with a full recovery anticipated, blood thinners will rule him out of contact activities until they are discontinued.
items.title: Jalen Hurts Expected to Miss Rest of 2026 NFL Season Due to Blood Clots

items.summary: The UK is paying record sums to maintain grid balance despite abundant domestic wind and solar generation, primarily due to transmission bottlenecks. While renewable capacity is concentrated in the north, demand centers lie in the south, creating a mismatch. On one day alone, urgent imports cost $51.2 million to balance the grid. Last month, the total grid balance bill reached an all-time high of 500 million pounds ($666 million). Experts note that building wind farms without considering consumption locations locks in these costs for generations. The only viable solution is expanding transmission infrastructure, though this poses financial challenges for consumers.
items.title: UK Pays Record Sums to Balance Grid as Transmission Falls Behind

items.summary: An analysis by FracTracker and Public Citizen reveals that Texas regulators continued processing permits for data center projects after Governor Greg Abbott ordered a halt. Despite Abbott's directive to pause approvals to assess impacts on water and grid stability, the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality processed 35 permitting actions in subsequent weeks. The groups noted that these actions allow development to proceed, contradicting the governor's intent. Abbott's office and the TCEQ did not immediately respond to requests for comment regarding the discrepancy between the pause order and ongoing regulatory activity.
items.title: Texas Regulators Continue Data Center Permits Despite Governor's Pause

items.summary: Difficult economic conditions and high prices in U.S. agriculture are creating barriers for the next generation of farmers. Many farmers are reaching retirement age, yet increasing volatility and sky-high prices make it tough for successors to take over the farms.
items.title: Agricultural Challenges Threaten Next Generation of U.S. Farmers

items.summary: US President Donald Trump criticized French President Emmanuel Macron regarding recent unrest in France, claiming Paris would soon become a Muslim city due to immigration. While Trump urged Macron to close borders, French authorities reported at least 2,400 arrests and damage to 3,000 businesses. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu defended the police response, noting no fatalities, while Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez resigned and later admitted authorities lost control in some cities.
items.title: Trump Accuses Macron of Failing to Stop France Riots Amid Immigration Claims

items.summary: Nikkei Inc. disclosed a third data breach in a month, exposing 1.83 million records. While most contained no identifying info, 150,000 records included names, emails, and addresses. The breach occurred on October 7 via stolen credentials accessing a development system. Nikkei revoked credentials, notified regulators, and stated no evidence of misuse or service outages as of October 16.
items.title: Nikkei Inc. Reports Third Data Breach Exposing 1.83 Million Records

items.summary: Americans will turn clocks back one hour on November 1, 2026, as Congress adjourned without passing legislation to end the twice-yearly time change. The proposed Sunshine Protection Act passed the House 301-117 in July but remains stalled in the Senate. President Donald Trump has urged lawmakers to end the practice, calling the system ridiculous, but federal law remains unchanged.
items.title: US Clock Change Stays in 2026 Despite House Vote

items.summary: Torrential rain killed at least four people in eastern Spain over recent days, sweeping away cars and submerging roads. Emergency crews conducted more than 400 rescues in Valencia, where rainfall reached 700 litres per square metre in 24 hours. Authorities ordered around 100 municipalities to remain indoors before lifting restrictions as conditions improved.
items.title: Torrential Rain Kills Four in Eastern Spain Floods

items.summary: A new wildlife overpass in Colorado has reduced wildlife-vehicle collisions by 91% since opening 10 months ago, according to a report. Officials track various species using the structure, which spans Interstate-25 between Denver and Colorado Springs. The project, funded by federal and state sources, aims to protect habitat and reduce crashes involving humans and animals.
items.title: Colorado Wildlife Overpass Reduces Vehicle Collisions

items.summary: Analysts compare HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank, noting that while HDFC remains larger by earnings, ICICI is expanding at almost twice the pace. ICICI reported a 20% year-on-year profit increase to Rs 14,800 crore, whereas HDFC's profit rose 5% to Rs 19,500 crore. Anand Rathi suggests HDFC has struggled to close the post-merger gap with ICICI across key metrics. Conversely, JM Financial values ICICI at a premium due to stronger growth and execution. HDFC Bank is valued lower, offering a potential recovery opportunity if margins bottom out and the growth gap narrows. Analysts highlight structural challenges for HDFC regarding deposits and funding costs.
items.title: Analysts Compare HDFC and ICICI Bank Growth and Valuation

items.summary: A Sydney court reviewed new video footage showing police using force during a protest against the visit of Israeli President Isaac Herzog. Defence lawyer Nick Hanna presented the clips to support a bid for documents, alleging unlawful arrests and excessive force. The footage includes scenes of officers moving worshippers during prayer. Trials for assault charges are expected in July 2027.
items.title: Court Sees New Footage of Police Force at Sydney Protest

items.summary: Andy Burnham announced new rules designed to outlaw unfair private parking charges, granting drivers a five-minute grace period to park and ten minutes to leave. While the government maintains a £100 maximum fine, the consumer group Which? criticized the measures as insufficient compared to their call for a £50 cap and an independent appeals body.
items.title: Andy Burnham announces new rules to curb private parking fines

items.summary: Andy Burnham announced new rules allowing drivers to challenge private parking charges and offering grace periods. The Prime Minister cited cases of unfair penalties, such as a £1,906 claim for a five-minute delay. While the RAC welcomes protections, some groups seek further reforms like banning debt recovery fees. The new code applies across England, Scotland, and Wales.
items.title: Burnham announces new rules to curb private parking charges

items.summary: Lokayukta police in Bhopal are investigating suspected links between a New Delhi transport company and former constable Saurabh Sharma regarding a disproportionate assets case. After 22 months without a chargesheet, officials found connections between Sharma and Chetan Singh Gaur. Over 60 people have been questioned, but police state it is premature to confirm a financial link, noting further investigation is required.
items.title: Lokayukta Police Investigate Asset Links in Saurabh Sharma Case

items.summary: Rank Math confirmed that downloads of its PRO plugin version 3.0.123 between October 15 and 16 contained malware capable of compromising websites. The vendor removed affected files and released a clean version 3.0.124. BleepingComputer identified connected indicators of compromise but could not confirm distribution through the plugin. Administrators are advised to restore from backups and rotate credentials.
items.title: Rank Math PRO Plugin Compromised in Supply-Chain Attack

items.summary: A US Church is positioned on the frontline of the fight against a new synthetic drug known as 'tranq'. While President Trump has previously labeled fentanyl a weapon of mass destruction, authorities now face evolving threats from strong animal tranquilizers. Although overdose deaths are falling, the increasing potency of these new substances worries recovery workers. Reporters Quentin Sommerville and Darren Conway traveled to Columbus, Ohio, to investigate the deepening crisis.
items.title: US Church Battles New Synthetic Drug Threat Known as Tranq

items.summary: Ukrainian tennis star Elina Svitolina announced the end of her marriage to Gaël Monfils, citing the emotional toll of the war in her country. In a heartfelt Instagram post, Svitolina described the conflict's internal impact and stated she could not remain in the marriage. Monfils, 40, was expected to play in the Paris Masters but has since retired to pursue a career in finance.
items.title: Elina Svitolina Announces Divorce From Gaël Monfils Citing War Impact

items.summary: An opinion piece argues that invading Iran would be a catastrophic strategic and moral error for the United States. The author contends that military reality, strategic blowback, and human costs make such an action indefensible. Citing wargames and recent air campaigns, the text suggests an invasion would fail and lead to endless occupation. It highlights global instability, rising oil prices, and the potential for Iran to unite behind its regime. The article concludes by urging Congress and the public to reject ground troops in Iran, emphasizing that America's strength lies in restraint and diplomacy rather than conquest.
items.title: Op-Ed Warns Against U.S. Invasion of Iran Citing Strategic Risks

items.summary: German startup NOVUS announced a new funding round to support expansion into the US in 2027 and European growth. The company's NOVUS One features a unique design with a large central opening, weighing 121 kg and offering a range of up to 150 km. While the current model starts at €21,300, a more affordable second model is planned for late 2027.
items.title: NOVUS Announces Funding for Electric Motorcycle Expansion

items.summary: Volkswagen opened orders for the entry-level ID. Cross electric SUV, starting at about $31,000. The vehicle features a 37 kWh battery and is described by CEO Thomas Schäfer as modern, reliable, and affordable. It is based on the MEB+ platform and will not be sold in the US.
items.title: Volkswagen Opens Orders for Affordable ID. Cross Electric SUV

items.summary: NTPC Limited, India's largest electric utility, signed a power purchase agreement with 247 Solar to deploy Concentrated Solar Power technology. This marks the first commercial project for 247 Solar, aiming to provide reliable, round-the-clock clean energy by overcoming solar intermittency. The ~1MW hybrid project is being installed at Rajasthan's Bhadla Solar Park, backed by the Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation Limited.
items.title: NTPC Signs PPA With 247 Solar for Advanced CSP Technology

items.summary: The Vatican reported that Pope Leo XIV held a call with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy regarding the city of Oleshky. During the conversation, the pontiff highlighted the serious situation there and urged for a humanitarian truce to facilitate food, medical aid, and the safe evacuation of civilians. This discussion occurred shortly after the Pope spoke with Russian leader Vladimir Putin.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Calls for Humanitarian Truce in Oleshky with Zelenskyy

items.summary: Environmental groups in Wyoming are debating the best approach to managing the rapid growth of data centers in the state. While outgoing Governor Mark Gordon signed an executive order to guide responsible development, concerns remain regarding water supply, electricity prices, and public lands. Organizations like The Sierra Club and The Wyoming Outdoor Council advocate for guardrails but disagree on a statewide moratorium. Some fear a temporary halt lacks a plan, while others worry local governments lack capacity for thorough review. Incidents in Cheyenne, such as a bacteria contamination and a request for backup generators, highlight the industry's scale and potential impacts. As new legislators arrive, environmental advocates urge a balanced approach to regulate this booming industry without stifling progress.
items.title: Wyoming Environmental Groups Debate Data Center Growth Management

items.summary: Global Guardian released the 2027 Global Risk Map, identifying rising security threats in Iran, Bahrain, Kuwait, Ecuador, Cuba, Jordan, Qatar, the UAE, and Saudi Arabia. The report also notes eased risks in Jamaica, South Korea, and Hungary. It highlights two major health emergencies and one major energy disruption as key developments for the coming year.
items.title: Global Guardian Maps 2027 Security Risks Across Six Nations

items.summary: Human Rights Watch accuses the Malian army, its Russian allies from Africa Corps, and armed jihadist groups of committing serious violations of international law against civilians. The organization is calling for urgent action from the African Union regarding these alleged crimes.
items.title: Human Rights Watch Accuses Mali Forces of Crimes Against Civilians

items.summary: The 17th U.N. Convention on Biological Diversity summit opened in Yerevan, highlighting that Africa requires an additional 15% of its terrestrial and marine territory to meet the 30 by 30 protection goal. While conservationists urge action, a review of ocean funding since 2014 revealed only $5.8 billion was delivered against $14.3 billion promised. The U.N. Secretary-General noted critical gaps in finance and capacity. Simultaneously, advocates warn that expanding protected areas without Indigenous involvement risks human rights violations, citing evictions in the Ngorongoro Conservation Area. African governments cite the failure of promised $20 billion in annual finance as a primary hurdle.
items.title: African Biodiversity Goals Face Funding and Rights Challenges at Yerevan Summit

items.summary: Felix Chen, Stephan Rabanser, Sayash Kapoor, and Arvind Narayanan from Princeton, along with collaborators from Stanford, the UK AI Security Institute, and Brookings, argue that the field of AI agent evaluation requires significant reform. The authors note that while AI developers frequently make claims based on benchmark scores, assessing the evidence supporting these claims is increasingly difficult. They emphasize that evaluators must scrutinize the entire trajectory of an agent, not just final outcomes, to account for shortcuts and attribution challenges. The paper highlights rising costs and the need for better tools, rigorous benchmarks, and a diverse set of independent evaluators to ensure validity and transparency in this fast-moving space.
items.title: Authors Call for Independent and Rigorous AI Agent Evaluation

items.summary: Early research suggests social media bans may not protect young people's mental health. While platforms face billions in lawsuits and over 20 countries are implementing bans, motivations vary. Governments cite mental health, privacy, and political concerns. Skeptics argue prohibiting access may not solve underlying issues, noting critics focus on developmental disruption rather than proving bans as a solution.
items.title: Research Questions Social Media Bans for Young People's Mental Health

items.summary: Japan successfully launched the H3 rocket carrying the Martian Moons eXploration probe early Tuesday from the Tanegashima Space Center. Developed by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency, the mission aims to retrieve samples from Mars' moons over five years to study the solar system's origins and potential for life on Earth. The probe separated from the rocket at 5:53 a.m.
items.title: Japan launches MMX probe to Mars moons for sample collection

items.summary: Cybersecurity firm Cyberpulse56 claims a significant data breach at State Bank of India (SBI), stating it is the first disclosure of the dataset. The group warned that if legitimate, the data could enable identity theft and financial fraud. SBI has not yet responded to inquiries from The Economic Times regarding the allegation.
items.title: Hacker group claims SBI data breach remains unverified

items.summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries and Ingeteam signed a memorandum of understanding to jointly develop energy infrastructure for US AI data centres. The partnership aims to address power quality and grid integration challenges associated with high-density computing. While the companies plan to expand technology availability, they have not disclosed specific projects or a deployment timetable, noting that opportunities remain subject to evaluation.
items.title: MHI and Ingeteam Partner on US AI Data Centre Power Solutions

items.summary: Chennai Police registered a case against DMK councillor Sudha Dheena Dayalan for derogatory remarks against Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay. During a speech, she called Vijay a 'dog' and compared his appearance to a dead body. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam demanded action, while Vijay stated that personal attacks against women would not be tolerated despite accepting political criticism.
items.title: Case Filed Against DMK Councillor for Abusive Remarks Against CM Vijay

items.summary: Mining activity in Bolivia's Yungas region threatens the habitat of the tilcayo, a wild cat species recently identified in the area. Despite a local law protecting the species, gold mining cooperatives and artisanal prospectors are expanding operations near Senda Verde Wildlife Refuge. The mining causes landslides, deforestation, and water contamination, displacing wildlife and endangering nearly 930 vertebrate species. Tensions have escalated between mining groups and conservationists, with some community members engaging in illegal extraction due to economic hardship. Authorities are struggling to enforce regulations as mining continues to encroach on protected areas.
items.title: Gold Rush Threatens Bolivia's Newly Discovered Wild Cat

items.summary: Several luxury stores in Milan's fashion district closed on Monday due to fears of renewed unrest following weekend looting and vandalism, according to ANSA. Stores including Chanel, Hermes, and Pomellato lowered their shutters while police were deployed. Italian Deputy Prime Minister Antonio Tajani expressed solidarity with affected merchants and law enforcement, promising a firm government response to attacks against the state.
items.title: Milan Luxury Stores Close Amid Fears of Renewed Unrest

items.summary: Christiane Amanpour announced she will leave CNN next June after 43 years as chief international anchor. She stated she will continue reporting through June 2027 and transition her interview program to a weekly format in January 2027. CNN Chairman Mark Thompson praised her legacy as one of the most trusted journalists.
items.title: Christiane Amanpour Announces Departure from CNN After 43 Years

items.summary: Nikole Hannah-Jones, a Pulitzer Prize-winning journalist and creator of the 1619 Project, argues that President Donald Trump effectively utilizes racial resentment to maintain power. Speaking at the Hay Festival in Dallas, she compares the segregation of first-class cabins to American society, suggesting Trump understands how to exploit white anxiety. Hannah-Jones notes that Trump's administration promotes a specific historical narrative to justify open racism. She also highlights the political consequences of her work, citing bans on the 1619 Project in Florida and Texas. Looking ahead to the midterm elections, she fears the administration will only accept outcomes favorable to its narrative.
items.title: Nikole Hannah-Jones Analyzes Trump's Use of Racial Resentment

items.summary: The BJP criticized Rahul Gandhi following reports of his trip to Vietnam, alleging he is meeting 'chaos collaborators' while the Congress party campaigns against the Chief Election Commissioner. Social media users shared viral clips claiming Gandhi traveled to Hanoi, though the Congress party has not confirmed the visit. BJP leaders questioned the timing and purpose of the alleged foreign journey.
items.title: BJP Criticizes Rahul Gandhi Over Reported Vietnam Trip Amid Political Campaign

items.summary: Nick Cammarata, a researcher at Goodfire, argues in a viral blog post that large language models may be easier to understand and control than previously believed. While some researchers celebrate the potential for better AI safety, others like Chris Potts and Jacob Hilton express skepticism, noting that understanding individual neurons does not yet equate to a full understanding of model circuits. Cammarata acknowledges the claims are not a complete solution but offers hope that the technology is fundamentally readable.
items.title: Researcher Claims Neural Networks Are More Understandable Than Thought

items.summary: A Special Executive Magistrate court extended judicial custody for two Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, by two days in connection with a trespassing case at Jantar Mantar. The court cited the leaders' 'habitualness' in organizing protests at de-notified sites and a lack of respect for the law. The order rejected their sureties due to discrepancies in documentation and noted that their assurances to adhere to terms were not credible. The CJP condemned the proceedings as a 'mockery of legal process' and a 'farce,' with legal head Ratna Singh stating that authorities failed to present evidence of a threat to public peace.
items.title: Court Extends Custody for CJP Leaders Over Jantar Mantar Protest

items.summary: North Sea workers are preparing to strike at oil rigs, potentially disrupting UK fuel supplies. The Unite union warns that a 24-hour strike could severely impact supplies. Apache and Harbour Energy blame the UK's tax regime for investment cuts. A third 48-hour strike is planned for 3 November.
items.title: North Sea strikes threaten UK fuel supplies amid union tensions
